Treatment summary
Patient presents following a motor vehicle collision in which their vehicle was struck
while turning left, with resulting right shoulder pain. The mechanism of injury is
consistent with the reported symptoms, and the pattern of complaints fits what would
be expected from this type of impact. Over the course of 18 visits, the patient
received conservative care including manual therapy, graded home exercise, and
anti-inflammatory medication. Treatment followed a typical progression, with visit
frequency reduced as symptoms improved and care tapered to discharge. Our assessment
relies largely on the patient's own description of pain and functional limitation, as
range of motion testing and orthopedic provocative maneuvers were within normal
limits, and imaging of the shoulder showed no acute abnormality. The patient reports a
remote minor strain to the same region in the past, which resolved completely without
lasting deficit. Billing records reflect single charges for each service with no
duplicated or repeated entries. Prognosis is good, and the pateint is discharged to
self-directed exercise with return to usual activities as tolerated.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
